title: User can still scroll, filter, and act on a Findings Register with 1000+ findings without the browser tab becoming unresponsive
description: End-to-end user-perspective companion to PERF-PERF-002: with no pagination or virtualization on FindingsRegisterTab.jsx (CustomTable.jsx pagination=false default), the risk is not just a slow initial render but the whole tab becoming sluggish for real interactions (filter, sort, open a finding).
preconditions: Real browser (not headless) for interaction-feel assessment
steps: Open the Findings Register tab for the seeded audit
Type into the search/filter box and observe input responsiveness (keystroke-to-render lag)
Click a column header to sort and time how long the table takes to re-render
Click into an individual finding to open its detail drawer
expectedResult: Filtering, sorting, and opening a finding each complete within 300ms of the user action with no visible input lag or dropped keystrokes. Document actual observed lag if it exceeds this and flag for remediation.

title: Risk Register triage queue paginates correctly across pages without re-fetching the full dataset
description: ModuleRiskTriageQueue.jsx (lines 558-752) is a correctly server-paged table (limit 10-100 via Pagination component, 7 columns) — a positive control for how paginated tables should behave, contrasted with the unpaginated Findings Register (PERF-E2E-001). Note fetchStats (line 305) separately fetches up to 500 rows client-side just to compute summary counts, which is not rendered but is a wasted payload worth measuring.
preconditions: Organization with 2,000+ risk-triage items across multiple modules
steps: Open the Module Risk Triage Queue and record the network payload size/timing for the first page load
Page forward through 5 pages and confirm each page issues its own bounded request rather than re-fetching everything
Inspect the network request triggered by fetchStats for its payload size
expectedResult: Each page navigation issues a small, bounded request (matching the selected page size). fetchStats's payload size is documented — flag if it exceeds 200KB or measurably delays the summary counts from appearing, as a candidate for a dedicated count/aggregate endpoint instead of fetching up to 500 full rows.

title: Notification bell reconnects and recovers missed notifications after a simulated network drop
description: NotificationContext.js initializes socket.io-client (lines 74-90) with reconnection:true, reconnectionAttempts:5, reconnectionDelay:2000, reconnectionDelayMax:10000, randomizationFactor:0.5. socket.js server-side also caches scan-progress snapshots in Redis with a 1-hour TTL (socket.js:254-260) for HTTP-polling recovery. This case verifies the client-visible reconnect behavior end to end.
preconditions: Logged-in session with the notification bell/Socket.IO connection established
Ability to simulate a network drop (DevTools offline mode or killing the WS connection)
steps: Confirm the Socket.IO connection is active (network tab shows an open WS/polling connection)
Simulate a network drop for 15 seconds (within the 5-attempt/10s-max backoff window)
Trigger a new notification from another session while the client was disconnected
Observe whether the notification bell updates once reconnected
expectedResult: The client automatically reconnects within the configured backoff window (observable in the network tab) and the unread count/notification list reflects the notification that was created while disconnected, without requiring a manual page refresh.

title: Unauthenticated visitor reaches a fully interactive first dashboard paint within budget after login
description: Full user-journey companion to PERF-PERF-006: from an unauthenticated landing page, through Keycloak login redirect, JWT verification (authenticate.js, lazy JWKS singleton with cache:true), permission load (loadPermissions.js, JIT provisioning path for brand-new users), to the first dashboard render.
preconditions: A brand-new, never-before-seen Keycloak user account
Browser performance timeline recording (Lighthouse or DevTools Performance tab)
steps: Start recording from the unauthenticated landing page
Complete Keycloak login as the brand-new user
Continue recording through redirect back to the app and the first dashboard render
Mark timestamps for: login submit, redirect received, first API response, dashboard fully interactive
expectedResult: Total time from login submit to a fully interactive dashboard is within 4 seconds on a typical broadband connection. Document actual timing breakdown per phase (auth redirect, JIT provisioning, first API calls, render) and flag whichever phase contributes disproportionately.

title: An uploaded evidence file becomes visible in the review queue within budget despite the evidence-risk-notify serialization point
description: End-to-end companion to PERF-PERF-004: the user-visible outcome of the 7-stage BullMQ pipeline (ingest -> validate -> normalize -> deduplicate -> store -> map -> risk-notify, conc=1 on the last stage) is when the evidence actually appears in the review queue, which depends on evidence-store/evidence-map, not the risk-notify stage — this case confirms the serialization bottleneck does not block user-visible availability even if it delays risk notifications.
preconditions: A burst of 50 other evidence uploads in flight from other users/orgs to create queue contention
steps: While 50 other uploads are being processed, upload one evidence file as the test user
Time from upload submission to the item appearing in the review queue with status 'Pending Review'
Separately, time from upload submission to any associated risk-notification event (if applicable) appearing
expectedResult: The evidence appears in the review queue within 30 seconds regardless of pipeline contention (store/map stages are not blocked by risk-notify's concurrency=1). If risk-notification is delayed significantly longer, document the delta but confirm it does not delay review-queue visibility, since these are independent downstream stages.
